notes.note_text_md: There is a lot of variation between dialects; West Saxon would have spelled this "seofedon", but here we have "seofedun"

This is a substantive adjective, which means it becomes a noun.   It is substative because it is genitive, but we have no noun that it modifies.  Since it is an adjective it should take the case of the noun it modifies, but mōd is accusative; hence "of the sea-weary."

sentences.text_modern:
No thought is in him to harp                           nor to receiving of rings -
nor in his delight in a woman                         nor in his hope in worldly things --
nor around aught of anything                         unless about surging of waves.
But always has longing                                  he who sets out into the sea.

annotation.modern_english_meaning: mind, spirit, intention, reason, thought, courage, ambition, pride

notes.note_text_md: nor in his delight in a woman
"nor in his trust/hope in the world (i.e. worldly things)".  This line is in effect parenthetical and "ne ymbe .. ġewealc" should be construed with "hyge" in  "Ne biþ him ... hringþege".

probobly the "longing" or "yearning" is for the onward journey and this half-line is a restatement of the seafarer's spiritual urge; but he michgt be making the point that, although he turns his back on earthly pleasures, he is still human enough to have longings.
